market_summary: Driver-level read of the broad-market basket: the dominant driver is trade-policy escalation -- Canada announced dollar-for-dollar tariff retaliation after talks collapsed, and the tape confirms it with cyclicals leading losses (XLI -3.4% on the week) while hedges rallied (GLD +5.5% w, XLE +2.8% w). The second driver is the rates path: the August PMI split (US services surging vs manufacturing contracting) keeps higher-for-longer alive, and rate-sensitive XLU was the week's worst sector at -3.5% (-2.3% Friday) while TLT was flat -- a de-rating of long-duration equities rather than a bond selloff. Equity beta held up comparatively well: SPY -1.4% w and QQQ -2.4% w after strong months (+3.6%/+4.3%), i.e. rotation out of cyclicals into real assets, not liquidation. Financials diverge positively: XLF is +11.5% over three months and still ground higher Friday (+0.9%).

top_story.headline: Canada to match U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar after trade talks collapse
top_story.why_it_matters: This is the week's decisive cross-asset driver: full retaliatory tariffs between the US and its largest trading partner directly pressure the industrial/cyclical leg of global equity exposure (XLI -3.4% w), lift demand for inflation and geo hedges (GLD's weekly acceleration alongside XLE strength), and add a policy wildcard on top of the September rate decision. Watch whether XLF's domestic-focused rally survives an escalation headline.

themes.title: Trade-policy shock: US-Canada tariff war escalates
themes.synthesis: The decisive driver of the week: dollar-for-dollar Canadian retaliation after collapsed talks hit trade-exposed cyclicals hardest -- industrials (XLI -3.4% w) led losses while the hedge complex bid up -- and it raises input-cost risk across globally-sourced supply chains into September.

themes.title: Rates path: two-speed economy keeps higher-for-longer alive
themes.synthesis: August flash PMIs split the economy -- services accelerating sharply while manufacturing contracts -- and the cross-asset signature says this is a duration story: utilities (XLU -7.6% m, -2.3% Friday) de-rated hard while long bonds (TLT flat w) held, meaning equities are repricing the discount rate faster than the bond market is.

themes.title: Real-asset bid: gold breaks out on hedging demand
themes.synthesis: Gold (+13.8% m, +5.5% w, +1.95% Friday) is the strongest trend in the universe, joined by energy (XLE +6.7% m), with metals-breakout calls citing currency concerns and Hormuz flow risk as supports -- a classic late-cycle hedge rotation that pairs with, and partially explains, the softness in rate-sensitive and cyclical equities.

themes.title: Positioning & flows: leverage rebuilt to pre-shock levels
themes.synthesis: CTA equity positioning has round-tripped to pre-Iran-shock levels while Treasury shorts stay stable per BofA -- systematic flows have limited dry powder to absorb another headline shock, which amplifies the tail risk around the tariff and rate events above.

outlook: Watch three drivers next week: (1) any US-Canada tariff follow-through -- XLI and XLF are the cleanest gauges inside this universe; (2) whether the XLU-vs-TLT spread keeps widening (duration de-rating without a bond rout) into the September decision; (3) if gold extends through its breakout while positioning is already back to pre-shock levels, that combination historically precedes volatility spikes.
